description: Every contributing deny-list is explicitly empty -- the union is [] and MUST stay [], not collapse to absent. Invisible to enforcement (neither hides anything) and NOT invisible to signing: an absent field is omitted from the canonical form while [] is emitted, so a policy authoring an empty hiddenObjects signed differently in Python than in .NET and TypeScript, and a context signed by one would not verify in the others. Found by porting purpose binding to Python; the cause was a truthiness retention check, which canonical-enforcement-spec.md section 3 names explicitly as the mistake to avoid. This fixture exists so the collapse cannot come back in any of the three languages -- and it covers hiddenObjects, deniedTags, readOnlyFields and hiddenEndpoints together, because one shared helper produced all four.
